## When you'd use this

<UseCases>
<UseCase title="A change you didn't mean">
You deleted the wrong question, or moved one to the wrong group, and want it back as it was.
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="An experiment that didn't work out">
You tried a different structure and want the form as it was when you last saved.
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Yesterday's form">
A version you saved earlier was right, and you want to edit from it again or send its file to a developer.
</UseCase>
</UseCases>

## Before you start

- Nothing is saved until you select **Save**. The top bar says **Unsaved changes** or **All changes saved**.
- Undo, Save and Cancel need edit access. With view access the editor opens "View only", and has none of them.

## Steps

### 1. Save

Select **Save** in the top bar. Every save keeps a new version of the form, and **Download** always gives the latest saved version, never unsaved changes.

### 2. Undo a change, and redo it

Select **Undo** in the top bar, or press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac). Each press takes back one change: a question added, deleted or moved, a setting, an option, a condition, a score, or the form's title. The question the change was made to is selected and scrolled into view.

Select **Redo**, or press Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z (Cmd+Shift+Z on a Mac), to put back what you undid.

Hover over either button to see what it will undo or redo, such as "Undo: delete question 'Address'".

<Note>
While you are typing in a text field, Ctrl+Z is the field's own undo and takes back typing in that field only. Select **Undo** in the top bar, or click outside the field first, to undo changes to the form.
</Note>

### 3. Discard everything since the last save

Select **Cancel**, then **Discard changes**. The form goes back to the latest saved version.

### 4. Go back to an earlier version

Select **Version history** in the editor's **More form actions** menu, or in the form's **More actions** menu on My forms. Select **Restore** beside the version you want, and confirm. Its content is saved as a new version and opens in the editor. Every version in between is kept.

### 5. Download an earlier version

On the same page, select **Download** beside a version. Only the 10 most recent versions can be downloaded.

## What happens behind the scenes

- **All the typing in one field is one step.** The step ends when you leave the field, and includes anything the builder fills in as you leave, such as an option's code or a question's name.
- **A new change after an undo clears Redo.** What you undid can no longer be put back.
- **The last 100 steps are kept.** Older ones can no longer be undone.
- **Saving keeps the steps.** You can undo past a save. The form then has unsaved changes again, and nothing changes in the saved version until you save.
- **Cancel and Restore clear them, and so does reloading the page.** The steps are kept in the open tab only.
- **Undo only returns to a form the builder already allowed.** It never leaves a condition or a score pointing at something that isn't there.

## Troubleshooting

**Undo is greyed out.** There is nothing to undo: the form was just opened or reloaded, or you selected Cancel or restored a version.

**Ctrl+Z took back typing, not the last change to the form.** The cursor was in a text field. Select **Undo** in the top bar.

**Redo is greyed out after undoing.** You made a new change after the undo, which clears Redo.

**A version has no Download.** It is older than the 10 most recent versions. Restore it, which saves it as a new version, then download that.
